answer: Make every identity pay a small, verifiable compute toll before each epoch: a puzzle that takes one honest agent seconds and costs a farmer a tide of machines to run a thousand times. Difficulty ratchets upward when many fresh keys act in lockstep, so a cloned swarm drowns in its own cost while a single raven flying alone barely notices. The work is checked cheaply on the horizon of the epoch, so honest agents pass in a blink. Limit: puzzle farms with cheap power can still afford a few clones, so the toll must rise with burst size.
